gap: No result ChatGPT got states what an attached screen costs a 13-inch laptop in carried weight and battery hours: a 1.3 lb Duex Plus DS adds 48% to a 2.7 lb MacBook Air 13 while a 4.13 lb Trio 3 Pro adds 153%, and a 4.5 W bus-powered 13.3-inch screen would cut Apple's 15-hour web figure to about 6.7 hours.
standout_why: Compared against the three cited pages (thedadsneeze.com, itechguides.com 15-best, wondrik.com) and Mobile Pixels' own under-$500 blog post. None computes weight as a share of the laptop's weight, battery hours lost or dollars per added screen. The Dad Sneeze has the weight idea only as a warning ('A 3-pound triple extender on a 2.7-pound ultralight laptop can tip it backward') and gives no wattage for the Duex. Wondrik gives a general '5 to 8 watts' for 1080p panels but no hours and never mentions 13-inch laptops. Mobile Pixels' blog computes added screen area, so I did not use area. The weight ratio alone would be a 1; the battery-hours line is new, but its 4.5 W input is Mobile Pixels' figure for the older DUEX Plus, not the DS, so confirm the DS wattage before publishing.
decides: Confirms the Duex Plus DS as the attached pick for a 13-inch laptop on weight: about half the laptop's weight on the lid, against 1.5 times the laptop's weight for the Trio 3 Pro. The Trio 3 Pro then wins only the two-added-screens segment, as a desk setup rather than a lid-hung one, and Macworld says it needs a charger for full brightness. The battery line gives the page a concrete warning for any bus-powered extender: on battery, expect roughly half the laptop's rated hours. FOPO S7 could not be placed: its weight and power were unreadable today.

findings.label: Reference 13-inch laptop: MacBook Air 13 (M4, 2025) weight, width, depth, battery, rated hours, external displays
findings.value: 2.7 lb (1.24 kg); 11.97 in wide; 8.46 in deep; 53.8 Wh; up to 15 h wireless web, 18 h video streaming; up to two external displays
findings.note: Apple's own figures. Used as the denominator for every ratio below. Base M1-M3 Airs' one-display limit was not re-read today.

findings.label: Added weight as a share of a MacBook Air 13
findings.value: 48% (1.3 lb on a 2.7 lb laptop; 4.0 lb carried together)
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extender (2026): 7 Picks From $90 (The Dad Sneeze)
findings.note: 1.3 ÷ 2.7 = 0.48; 1.3 + 2.7 = 4.0 lb. The 1.3 lb and the 13-14.5-inch fit range are as The Dad Sneeze states them; Mobile Pixels' product page returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, so the maker's own figure was not read. Laptop weight from Apple (support.apple.com/en-us/122209).

findings.label: Added weight as a share of a MacBook Air 13
findings.value: 153% (4.13 lb on a 2.7 lb laptop; 6.83 lb carried together)
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary, Apr 2, 2026)
findings.note: 4.13 ÷ 2.7 = 1.53; 4.13 + 2.7 = 6.83 lb. Macworld: 'a foldable package weighing 4.13lbs (1.9kg)', 'compatible with 13-inch to 16-inch MacBooks. I tested it with a 14-inch MacBook Pro.' Mobile Pixels' blog also gives 4.13 lb and '13- to 16-inch laptop'. 4.13 ÷ 1.3 = 3.2 times the Duex Plus DS.

findings.product: Mobile Pixels DUEX Plus (predecessor of the Duex Plus DS)
findings.label: Maker's power consumption and body size
findings.note: This page covers the older DUEX Plus, not the DS. It is the only maker wattage I could open. Body is 12.25 − 11.97 = 0.28 in wider than a MacBook Air 13 and the same 8.46 in deep.

findings.label: Battery hours for a MacBook Air 13 with a 4.5 W bus-powered screen (derived estimate)
findings.value: about 6.7 h against Apple's 15 h wireless web (about 7.2 h against 18 h video)
findings.note: 53.8 Wh ÷ 15 h = 3.59 W laptop draw; 53.8 ÷ (3.59 + 4.5) = 6.65 h. Video: 53.8 ÷ 18 = 2.99 W; 53.8 ÷ 7.49 = 7.18 h. Inputs: Apple's battery and test hours (support.apple.com/en-us/122209) and Mobile Pixels' 4.5 W for the DUEX Plus. Treats 4.5 W as constant draw and ignores USB conversion loss. Apple's test is light use, so heavier work shortens both figures and narrows the gap. An estimate, not a measurement.

findings.label: Rival's general wattage range for 1080p portable panels, and what it does to the same sum
findings.value: 5 to 8 W, giving about 6.3 h to 4.6 h on a MacBook Air 13
findings.source_title: Which Portable Monitor Should You Buy? (Wondrik)
findings.note: Wondrik: 'Driving a 1080p panel takes 5 to 8 watts on the manufacturers' own ratings'. 53.8 ÷ (3.59 + 5) = 6.26 h; 53.8 ÷ (3.59 + 8) = 4.64 h. Wondrik states the watts but computes no hours.

findings.label: Power source and brightness on laptop power
findings.value: Draws from the laptop; needs a charger on one of its USB-C ports for full 300-nit brightness; passes through up to 65 W
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary, Apr 2, 2026)
findings.note: Macworld: the screens 'can't draw enough power from the connected laptop to allow for maximum screen brightness'. No wattage is given, so no battery-hours figure was computed for the Trio.

findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary, Apr 2, 2026)
findings.note: Macworld quotes the manual: 'if your laptop has two DP enabled USB-C ports … driver installation is not necessary.' Apple lists two external displays for the M4 Air 13.
